contradictions.summary: Self-describes as budget-conscious with ₹250 max, but reveals spending ₹4500 on cologne and willingness to pay ₹400-500 for office deodorant

claim_a.label: stated
claim_a.speaker: user
claim_a.verbatim: Dekho normally I say budget-conscious hoon. ₹250 max.

claim_b.label: revealed
claim_b.speaker: user
claim_b.verbatim: Cologne hai mere paas. Hugo Boss Bottled, that was ₹4500. But that's for special occasions, dates, parties. Duty free se liya tha when I went to Dubai.
claim_b.summary_role: reveals 18x spend on fragrance in different context

contradictions.rationale: The 'budget-conscious' identity is a category-specific framing, not an absolute trait. Customer compartmentalizes: deodorant = commodity (₹250), cologne = aspirational (₹4500), office deo = professional tool (₹400-500). The stated price sensitivity is conditional on perceived product category, not inherent frugality. This suggests price ceiling is repositionable through category reframing.
contradictions.actionability_hint: Premium SKU positioned closer to 'cologne' or 'professional fragrance' category could unlock ₹400-500+ price acceptance in same customer segment

contradictions.summary: Describes Wildstone experience as 'overall achha hai' but immediately lists significant functional failures

claim_a.label: stated
claim_a.speaker: user
claim_a.verbatim: Overall achha hai but kuch issues hain.
claim_a.summary_role: frames experience as generally positive with minor issues

claim_b.label: revealed
claim_b.speaker: user
claim_b.verbatim: First thing, packaging. The cap doesn't click shut properly yaar. I've had it open in my gym bag and leak twice now.
claim_b.summary_role: reveals product failure causing functional damage

contradictions.rationale: Politeness framing ('overall achha hai') immediately collapses into concrete product failures (leaking, cap malfunction). The customer's 'kuch issues' minimizes what are actually significant functional problems — a cap that doesn't seal is not a minor issue for a gym-bag product. Social desirability bias leads with positive framing before truth emerges.
contradictions.actionability_hint: Customer satisfaction surveys likely understate packaging complaints due to politeness bias; qualitative probing reveals severity

contradictions.summary: Cites scent as primary reason for loyalty, but has already switched to competitor for primary use case (office)

claim_a.label: stated
claim_a.speaker: user
claim_a.verbatim: Honestly the smell I liked. Ultra Sensual, Bombshell, those scents are like... they have character. Axe felt very teenage, you know? But Wildstone feels more grown up, more masculine.
claim_a.summary_role: positions scent as key differentiator and loyalty driver

claim_b.label: revealed
claim_b.speaker: user
claim_b.verbatim: Yeah recently I bought Nivea Men Cool Kick for office use. That one I keep on my office desk. It's lighter, more subtle, more professional smell. Wildstone weekend pe use karta hoon, gym mein, casual outings.
claim_b.summary_role: reveals Nivea is now primary weekday product, Wildstone relegated to weekends

contradictions.rationale: Scent is praised as the differentiator, but the same strong scent is why customer has switched to Nivea for office (likely 5 days/week). The feature that drives stated loyalty is also the feature causing behavioral defection. Wildstone is being relegated to secondary/weekend use while Nivea captures the high-frequency office occasion.
contradictions.actionability_hint: Strong scent is a double-edged sword — drives differentiation but limits use occasions. Subtle variant captures the weekday volume customer is already giving to Nivea
